title: Late discharge summaries
topic: Responding to criticism, feedback and your own underperformance
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the acute medical unit. Your consultant tells you that several of your discharge summaries have been sent days late, and a GP has complained that a patient's medication change wasn't communicated in time.

You've been busy and have been leaving summaries until the end of the week.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Ask which cases were affected, and what happened.
options.brief: Understanding what happened helps you change.
options.detailed: Knowing which summaries were late, and the consequences, helps you see why it matters.

options.text: Explain that you've been too busy to write them sooner.
options.brief: True, but doesn't address the problem.
options.detailed: Workload is real, but late summaries affect patients' care.

options.text: Write summaries on the day of discharge from now on.
options.detailed: Writing summaries on the day of discharge, even briefly, means GPs get the information when they need it.

options.text: Write shorter summaries, leaving out medication changes.
options.detailed: This saves time but leaves out the most important information.

options.text: Ask your supervisor for advice on managing your time.
options.brief: Support with workload and time management.
options.detailed: Your supervisor can suggest strategies and help if your workload is genuinely too high.

options.text: Ask the F1 to write your summaries.
options.brief: Shifts the problem to a colleague.
options.detailed: This doesn't solve the problem and adds to the F1's workload.

options.text: Stay late every night until all summaries are done.
options.brief: Unsustainable, and doesn't fix the routine.
options.detailed: This may help for a while but isn't sustainable.

options.text: Apologise to the consultant, and carry on as before.
options.brief: An apology without change doesn't help.
options.detailed: Acknowledging the problem is good, but nothing changes.

explanation.issue: This tests how you respond to feedback about your own work, by understanding the impact and changing your practice.
explanation.keyDetails: Summaries were late. A medication change wasn't communicated. You've been leaving them until the end of the week.
explanation.reasoning: [A] understands the impact, [C] changes your routine, and [E] gets support. The distractors excuse it ([B]), compromise safety ([D]), shift it ([F]), are unsustainable ([G]), or don't change anything ([H]).
explanation.competing: [G] is the tempting option, but it doesn't change the routine that caused the problem.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 1, reflecting on feedback; Domain 3, communicating with colleagues who share care.
